title: Risk Dovetail: SOC2 prep scratchpad
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Personal scratchpad for stitching together control evidence and risk questions for our upcoming SOC2 readiness check. Not official — this is the working surface before I move things into the evidence catalog.
- Focus areas this week: access reviews, secrets rotation, incident logging completeness, and dedupe of overlapping runbooks.

High level observations (working hypotheses):
- Most infra controls have artifacts, but there is inconsistent retention windows across services (S3 vs. logging infra). Risk: auditor will flag incomplete retention or missing retention policy documentation.
- Manual access reviews exist but are not centralized; product teams do ad-hoc offboarding notes in Slack. Risk: evidence trail gap.
- We have automated rotation for service keys in k8s, but some legacy VM services still use long-lived creds. Action: enumerate, prioritize high-priv keys.

Quick wins to capture first (low effort, high signal):
- Snapshot of IAM group membership + timestamped export (console + csv) for critical groups (admins, infra-deploy, db-admin). Owner: Ava. Due: 2026-02-16.
- Add evidence note to confluence page for retention policy (point to S3 lifecycle, Cloud Logging retention). Owner: me. Due: 2026-02-18.
- Pull a 30-day incident log extract (pagerduty + opsgenie ticket list) and tag with incident class (security/availability/ops). Owner: Noah. Due: 2026-02-20.

Open questions / follow-ups (things I need to ask people):
- Does infra team have any undocumented service accounts? (Ping: @infra-oncall channel, ask for service-account inventory)
- Where are internal runbooks stored for DB failover? Confluence link seems stale. Could product SRE point to canonical?
- For Dedicated customers, are there separate KMS keys noted in CMDB? Need to capture customer-managed KMS evidence if present.

Rough control mapping (very draft):
- CC: Access controls (logical): evidence = IAM export, SSO logs, provisioning tickets. Owner: infra. Gap: offboarding ticket indexing.
- CC: Change management: evidence = PRs + release notes + change approvals. Owner: release-engineering. Gap: automated snapshot linking PR -> deployment for some pipelines.
- CC: Logging & monitoring: evidence = Cloud Logging retention policy, alerts, runbook snapshots, incident postmortems. Owner: SRE/observability. Gap: alert-to-ticket mapping inconsistent.

Evidence inventory (brain dump):
- IAM group exports (console CSV) — include date/time on export.
- SSO provider audit logs (Okta) — challenge: export format and retention.
- Secrets manager rotation logs (HashiVault/Cloud KMS) — include rotate event IDs.
- CI pipeline: PR -> build -> deploy trace (Circle/GH Actions logs).
- Backup verification reports (DB snapshots + restore test notes).
- Incident postmortems: link to confluence pages (label with incident id).
- Personnel training signoffs (phishing / secure coding) — HR CSV.

Evidence packaging notes (how I want to present to auditor):
- Each control should have 1 paragraph summary + 2 primary artifacts + 1 cross-check (logs or ticket).
- Prefer timestamped exports (screenshot alone is weak). If screenshot only, accompany with explanation why no export exists and timeline to add export.

Risk scoring shorthand (0-5):
- Retention policy inconsistency: 3 (path to fix clear but needs coordination).
- Undocumented service accounts: 4 (elevated risk, need immediate inventory).
- Manual offboarding evidence: 3 (process exists but evidence scattered).
- Secrets long-lived creds: 4 (mitigate by rotation schedule and blocking access).

Action items (current board):
- Inventory VMs with static keys (script recommended). Owner: Sasha. ETA: 2026-02-24.
- Centralize offboarding checklist template into HR-Confluence page and link to onboarding/offboarding workflows. Owner: People Ops + infra. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- Add retention policy table to confluence and map to log buckets/services (explicit links + S3 lifecycle rules). Owner: Sasha. ETA: 2026-02-18.

Notes to self (implementation quirks / TL;DRs):
- When pulling Okta logs, prefer syslog export + gzip to keep auditor-friendly format.
- For PR -> deploy mapping: tag release artifacts with PR numbers and record deploy timestamps; export via API to create crosswalk.
- If a team refuses to provide CSVs, request a read-only link to their admin console for auditor access (last-resort).

Potential blockers / escalation points:
- Lack of capacity on infra to run inventory scripts — may need solutions eng support.
- HR data request delays (training CSV) — escalate to People Ops lead.
- Customer-managed KMS evidence may need legal review before sharing.

Conversation snippets (copy/paste from Slack I want to capture):
- "we rotated the postgres key last quarter but didn't record rotation id" — capture and follow up with dev team to export rotation event.
- "DB failover runbook is in PJ's drive, not confluence" — coordinate owner change and canonicalization.

Hypothesis for next audit prep sprint (what to aim to close):
- Close evidence trails for access reviews and retention policies first (they give highest confidence).
- Second sprint: secrets + service account inventory.
- Third sprint: change management traceability and PR->deploy linking.

Final quick checklist before I move curated artifacts to confluence: (one-pass)
- [ ] Timestamped export for each artifact
- [ ] Short summary paragraph for control (who, what, why)
- [ ] Cross-reference to ticket/PR/incident
- [ ] Owner assigned and contact info

TODO (immediate):
- Run IAM group export (admins + infra-deploy) and drop in /confluence/drafts (me).
- Slack @infra-oncall: request service-account inventory script or list.
- Email People Ops: ask for training CSV and retention policy for HR data.

End of scratchpad. This is messy — clean up into the evidence catalog once the quick wins are done.

-- Sasha

(Edits log: initial notes 2026-02-10; added quick wins 2026-02-12; updated blockers + timeline 2026-03-04)
